primary_objective: Develop an industry-oriented application managing the complete lifecycle: Report - Classify - Prioritize - Assign - Investigate - Resolve - Verify - Close using sound OOP principles.
fourteen_step_scenario: 14. Include the incident in relevant reports and analytics

mvp_requirements.notification: At least two notification mechanisms (simulated or real)
mvp_requirements.search_and_reporting: At least five meaningful search/filter criteria + overview/workload/service reports

three_mandatory_workflows.workflow_1: Employee reports -> system classifies/prioritizes -> technician assigned -> notification generated
three_mandatory_workflows.workflow_2: Technician investigates -> SLA monitored -> incident resolved -> user notified
three_mandatory_workflows.workflow_3: Multiple incidents reported -> duplicates/related identified -> correlated/escalated

oop_design_requirements: Encapsulation: Data protected through appropriate access mechanisms
Abstraction: Complex business operations represented through suitable abstractions
Inheritance: Used only where an appropriate is-a relationship exists
Composition: Collaboration through composition where appropriate
Association and Aggregation: Demonstrated between domain objects
Exception Handling: Handling invalid situations with custom exceptions
Collections / Data Structures: Selected based on application requirements
Design Patterns: At least two design patterns implemented
tech_selection_report_questions: Q1. Why did you choose this programming language?
Q2. Why did you choose this frontend technology?
Q3. Why did you choose this backend technology?
Q4. Why did you select this database?
Q5. Why did you choose this architecture?
Q6. What alternatives did you consider?
Q7. What are the advantages and limitations of your technology stack?
Q8. How does your technology support object-oriented design?
Q9. How would your system evolve if the number of users increased significantly?
testing_requirements: At least 15 meaningful test cases covering normal operations, boundary conditions, invalid inputs, exceptions, authorization, business rules

rubric.desc: Problem understanding and clear prototype development
Working implementation of mandatory modules (refer MVP)
Code quality, APIs, third-party services, scalability of design
Unit testing, integration testing, edge cases, exception handling
Going beyond basic requirements with intelligent features
Completeness of report, clarity, and effectiveness of demo video
